intended_object: The standard bijection between the symmetric group S_k and the Brauer diagrams on k strands in which every arc is a through strand (no caps or cups). Each permutation σ goes to the diagram joining bottom point i to top point σ(i). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
A Brauer diagram is defined as a perfect matching (a fixed-point-free involution) of `Fin k ⊕ Fin k`. `IsThrough x` says that `x` is matched with a point on the other boundary. The forward map, `permToBrauer σ`, sends `inl i` to `inr (σ i)` and `inr j` to `inl (σ⁻¹ j)`. This is exactly the usual permutation diagram, and every arc in it is a through strand. The inverse map reads σ(i) off as the top point matched with bottom point i. Both round-trip identities are proved, so this is the expected bijection S_k ≃ {diagrams with no horizontal arcs}.

Using `Fin k` is the standard indexing for Brauer diagrams on k strands, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no Brauer diagrams, so it has no counterpart.
